title: Lesson 1-4: Measures of Central Tendency
p: Enter your full name below, and press the enter button next to the text field, so I can track who has completed this assignment and who has not. These assignments in Doenet are not connected to OAKS.

The lessons below will help you learn about measures of central tendency and the different types of measures available, along with advantages and disadvantages of each. At the conclusion of the lesson, you should be comfortable with the following topics:
Understanding how a mean, median, and mode are calculated
Understanding the difference between a mean and weighted mean, and how to calculate a weighted mean
Understadning when it is appropriate to use a mean, versus a median or mode
How to calculate a mean and median using your chosen class technology
How to calculate a weighted mean using your chosen class technology

The total video run-time for all 9 videos is approximately 45 minutes. To complete the videos, and answer the questions, you should budget about 1.5 - 2 hours. The homework in XYZ will require at least an additional hour.

The last three videos give you a choice to view the examples performed using a TI calculator, or the online Stats Calculator that I developed for the class. To get a full grade in this lesson, you do not need to watch both sets of options, only the ones that correspond to your chosen technology.

choiceInput.label: What is true about the calculation of a population mean?
choiceInput.choice: The calculation of a population mean and sample mean is identical
The population mean is calculated by dividing the sum of the data by one less than the number of data items.
The population mean requires you to square each data item before adding the set together.
The population mean requires you to remove the largest and smallest data item before adding together the values in the data set.

cascade.exercise:
Question 7
If the maximum value in a data set is replaced with a value that is larger, what would be the effect on the median?
The new median would be smaller in value The new median would be larger in value The median would be unaffected It would be impossible to determine
<feedback condition="$q7.creditAchieved < 1"> If you replace the largest value in a data set with an even larger value, this will have no effect on the median. This is because the median is designed to be unaffected by outliers and the largest (and smallest) values in a data set are the most likely to be outliers.
